question: Bhupesh suffered crop failure for few years. When he got the pH of the soil examined, it was about 11.6. Which of the following compounds can he use to treat the soil of his agricultural field?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Al**____**2(SO4)3 **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhupesh's agricultural **field has soil of pH 11.6** which is **basic **in character.

 
 
• He will **need to add some acidic salt decrease the pH of soil for better crop**.
 
 
 
• **Aluminum sulfate (Al2(SO4)3)** is a salt formed by reaction of aluminum hydroxide (a base) with sulfuric acid.
 
 
• Since aluminum hydroxide is a weak base and sulfuric acid is a strong acid, the **salt is acidic**.
 
• Thus aluminum sulfate is an acidic salt.
 
 
 
• So, the best option for him is to **add Aluminum sulfate (Al2(SO4)3****) in his field**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)**, also known as **slaked lime **is a source of hydroxide ions when dissolved in aqueous solutions.

 
 
• Therefore, this compound is a **base**.​
 
 
 
• **NaCl (Sodium chloride) **is a salt that doesn't show acidic or basic nature.
 
 
• It is **neutral **with a pH of about 7.
 
• It is made with the combination of hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
 
• Both of them having a strong nature, neutralizes each other and produces neutral salt NaCl and water.
 
 
 
• **Zinc hydroxide (Zn(OH)2 )** is a slightly soluble salt but is also a **base**.
 
 
• This level of insolubility makes zinc hydroxide a weak electrolyte. Since it is a weak electrolyte, it is also a weak base.
